documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six-month check on the prednisone. Feels well. No bleeding this year. Hematology in February: count around 40, no change. Weight up a little more, about 71 kg; she's been less active this spring with indoor recess duty and wants to get back to walking. No thirst, no vision change, sleep fine taking it in the morning.

Exam: BP normal. Few small bruises on the shins. No cushingoid features. No edema.

A/P
1. Chronic ITP, hematology managing, prednisone 10 mg daily.
2. Steroid effects: weight creeping up, otherwise nothing. A1c was 5.4 in November, DXA normal 2021. Walking plan. Labs at the physical in the fall.
RTC fall physical.

documents.title: Call - face drooping
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called from home before school: woke up and the right side of her face feels heavy, can't close the right eye all the way, drink dribbles from the right side. No arm or leg weakness, no trouble speaking or seeing, no headache. Discussed with PCP; same-day slot at 11:20. Told to call 911 for any limb weakness, speech or vision change.

documents.title: Office Visit - Same Day
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Woke this morning with the right side of her face not working. Can't shut the right eye fully, can't lift the right brow, smile pulls to the left. Had a cold last week, now gone. No rash, no ear pain, no hearing change. No tick bites she knows of, hasn't been hiking. No limb weakness or numbness, no speech or swallowing trouble, no headache. ITP on prednisone 10 mg, no recent bleeding.

O: Vitals as charted. Right lower motor neuron facial weakness: forehead does not wrinkle on the right, incomplete right eye closure with Bell's phenomenon, flattened right nasolabial fold, mouth pulls left. Left face normal. Ear canals and TMs normal, no vesicles. No rash. Other cranial nerves intact. Strength, sensation, coordination and speech normal in all four limbs.

A/P: Acute right peripheral facial weakness, forehead involved, otherwise normal neuro exam; pattern fits Bell's but she is on chronic prednisone with ITP, so I'd like neurology to see her promptly. Called the neurology office, they will see her Thursday. Eye care today: lubricating drops several times a day, tape the eye shut at night, wraparound glasses outside. ED for any new neurologic symptom. Out of school through Thursday.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily for 10 days in place of the usual 10 mg dose, then resume 10 mg daily
1 drop in the right eye every 2 to 4 hours while awake
Apply to the right eye at bedtime, then tape the eye closed

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY PRACTICE
New consultation, seen 09/21/2023
Referred by: primary care, urgent

44-year-old right-handed teacher with chronic ITP on prednisone 10 mg daily, referred for right facial weakness that began on waking two days ago. She cannot shut the right eye, lift the right eyebrow or make an even smile. A cold settled shortly before. No rash, ear pain or tick exposure.

Meds: prednisone 10 mg daily, calcium carbonate 600 mg TID, vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: complete paralysis of the right side of the face, upper and lower, with incomplete eye closure. No vesicles in the ear or palate. Remaining cranial nerves normal. Limb strength and sensation normal; reflexes symmetric; gait normal.

Impression: right Bell palsy (idiopathic peripheral facial palsy), within 72 hours of onset.

Plan:
1. Prednisone 50 mg daily for 10 days, taken instead of her usual 10 mg, then back to 10 mg. Discussed with her hematology group, who agree.
2. Eye protection: carboxymethylcellulose drops to the right eye every 2 to 4 hours while awake; gel at bedtime and tape the lid shut; glasses outdoors.
3. No imaging now. Revisit if no improvement by 3 months or if anything atypical appears.
4. Follow up in 6 to 8 weeks.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks into the right Bell palsy. Neurology saw her 9/21: prednisone 50 mg x10 days in place of the 10 mg, finished 9/30, now back on 10 mg. Eye drops and nightly gel and taping. Slowly coming back: she can almost close the eye now and the smile is a bit more even. Eye not painful or red. Back at school since 9/25. Some trouble sleeping on the higher dose, now settled.

Exam: right facial weakness improving, partial movement of the right brow and mouth, eye closes with a small gap. Conjunctiva quiet. Rest of neuro exam normal.

A/P
1. Right Bell palsy, recovering. Keep eye care until closure is complete. Neurology follow-up in November.
2. Chronic ITP, prednisone back to 10 mg.
3. Flu vaccine today.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
44 y/o for her yearly.

Interval: right Bell palsy in September, prednisone burst from neurology, fully recovered per their November note and her own sense. ITP quiet all year on prednisone 10 mg, last hematology in June, next in December. Calcium and D continue.

ROS: no bleeding, no headaches, no vision change. Mood good.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight steady around 71. Face symmetric, eye closure complete. Skin with a couple of small bruises. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, no splenomegaly. Breast exam normal. Pelvic: cervix normal appearing, Pap/HPV collected.

A/P
1. Bell palsy, resolved, off the active list.
2. Chronic ITP on prednisone 10 mg, CBC for hematology's December visit.
3. Steroid monitoring: A1c, CMP, vitamin D.
4. Health maintenance: Pap with HPV today (5 years). Mammogram October normal. Flu 10/5, COVID 10/26. Colon cancer screening starts at 45, next year.
RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPT - PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrived 03/28/2024 09:10

CC: vertigo with nausea and vomiting for 2 days.

HPI: 44 yo F with chronic ITP on prednisone 10 mg daily and a prior right Bell palsy (2023, recovered). Room-spinning dizziness came on suddenly two days ago and has not let up; with it nausea and repeated vomiting, unable to work or manage at home. A cold cleared about a week ago. No hearing loss, no ringing in the ears. No headache, double vision, slurred speech, limb weakness or numbness.

Meds: prednisone 10 mg daily, calcium carbonate 600 mg TID, vitamin D3 2000 IU daily. Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: within normal limits.
Exam: uncomfortable, nauseated. Spontaneous nystagmus, increasing on leftward gaze. Romberg positive. Dix-Hallpike attempted but she could not tolerate it because of nausea. Remaining neurologic exam nonfocal: cranial nerves otherwise intact, strength and sensation normal, no dysmetria. Hearing grossly intact. TMs normal.

ED course: ondansetron 4 mg IV and meclizine 25 mg PO, with improvement in nausea; tolerated fluids by mouth.

Impression: vestibular neuritis.
Dispo: home. Meclizine 25 mg every 8 hours as needed and ondansetron ODT 4 mg every 8 hours as needed, a few days' supply. Return for severe headache, weakness, trouble speaking or walking, or inability to keep fluids down. Follow up with PCP this week.

documents.title: ER yesterday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I was in the ER yesterday with terrible dizziness and throwing up. They said it's an inner ear nerve inflammation and gave me meclizine and a nausea pill. Still pretty dizzy but not vomiting. Can I see you next week? I'll need a note for school too.

documents.title: Re: ER yesterday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sorry you went through that. I have the ER record. Front desk will set you up Tuesday. Use the meclizine only when you need it; it can slow recovery if you take it around the clock for many days. Let me know right away if you get a bad headache, weakness, or trouble talking or walking.

documents.title: Office Visit - ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED 3/28 for vestibular neuritis: two days of sudden constant vertigo with vomiting after a cold, no hearing loss. Much better now. Stopped the ondansetron Saturday and the meclizine yesterday. Left with a bit of imbalance turning her head quickly.

Exam: vitals as charted. No spontaneous nystagmus today. Gait steady, can tandem walk slowly. Cranial nerves intact, face symmetric. Strength normal.

A/P: vestibular neuritis, recovering. Home balance and gaze exercises handout reviewed. Back to teaching next Monday; note given. Message me in a few weeks with an update, sooner if worse.

documents.title: Dizziness update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Just following up like you asked. The dizziness is gone. I did the exercises for a couple of weeks and now I don't notice anything, even on the playground.

documents.title: Re: Dizziness update

documents.body: Great news. I'll mark the vestibular neuritis as resolved. See you in the fall.

45 y/o yearly visit.

Interval: vestibular neuritis in March, ED, recovered by end of April. ITP stable, hematology in June with no changes; next in December. Still prednisone 10 mg daily, calcium carbonate, D3. No bleeding episodes this year.

ROS: negative. No dizziness. Face normal. Mood good.

Exam: vitals as charted. Face symmetric. No nystagmus. Skin with scattered small bruises on shins. Heart RRR, lungs clear, abdomen soft without splenomegaly. Breast exam normal. No edema.

A/P
1. Chronic ITP, prednisone 10 mg via hematology. CBC today.
2. Steroid monitoring: A1c, CMP. Vitamin D fine last year.
3. Colorectal screening now that she is 45: talked through colonoscopy versus yearly FIT; with her platelets she prefers to start with FIT. Kit given.
4. Mammogram October normal. Flu 10/10, COVID 10/17. Pap 2023.
RTC 1 year.
